the mouse off the food selector panicked. BallFish shares Breeder's coin value function. A
fish with a taste for prey (e.g. one that eats Ultravores) runs Fish::Eat on the creature it
ate; Eat read the food's kind and grade, which panicked on a creature. It now reads the same
offsets the original does from the creature (eaten_word).

Rewrite the README for the current port

Organized for players first (what's new, requirements, build and play, controls, settings,
HD art, debug menu), then developers. Also fixes the mangled registry.ini path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep the settings between launches; remember the window size and position

The replaced registry was never written to disk, so full screen, volumes and the other
settings reset every launch. It is now kept as userdata/registry.ini (loaded before
ReadFromRegistry, rewritten on change). The host also saves the window's size and position
and restores them at boot. The close button now runs the game's Shutdown (as WM_CLOSE did),
and the final saves are written before the process exits.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Centre the store's dialogs; Escape opens the pause menu; middle click toggles hold-to-collect

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Debug menu: hold the left button to collect money under the cursor (9)

While on, each frame the button is held in a running tank, every uncollected item under the

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Run logic updates at the app's mFrameTime (28 ms), not 10 ms

WinFishApp's constructor sets mFrameTime (+0x44c) to 28, and SexyAppBase::Process runs one
update per mFrameTime. The host used the framework default of 10 ms, so the game ran 2.8x
too fast. The debug menu now shows game updates per second.

Merge pull request #3 from ITSTDMCC/hd-art

The HD update

HD art is opt-in (--hd); step-by-step HD setup in the README

The game uses its original art unless started with --hd (or WINFISH_HD=1). Play HD.bat
starts it with HD art.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

HD art for the whole game

The HD screen is used on every screen. upscale_art.py defaults to every image and font.
The HD picture is uploaded as BGRA (no conversion) and only after a redraw, which keeps tanks
at 60 fps. Images the game draws into or cuts at runtime drop their HD art. Opaque bilinear
samples take an integer path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Load HD art per image on worker threads, not in the launch read

The hd folder is skipped when the game folder is read at launch. When the game loads an
image (G::alloc), its HD art is decoded on a worker thread, so a screen's art is ready by the
time the screen shows; it is dropped after the image is freed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

HD art for the interface: dialogs, buttons, checkboxes, sliders and fonts

upscale_art.py reads properties/resources.xml for each image's alpha mask and adds a 'ui'
set; hd.rs only uses art whose transparency matches the image it replaces.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

HD main menu from player-made upscaled art

tools/upscale_art.py upscales the main menu images 4x with Real-ESRGAN into <game>/hd/images
(from the player's own copy; no art in the repo). While the main menu is up, src/sexy/hd.rs
paints the frame's blitter calls onto a 4x screen using that art, and the host displays it.
The 640x480 screen is unchanged. WINFISH_NO_HD=1 turns it off.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

GIF transparent pixels decode as 0, like the original loader

Alpha images such as _SLIDERWIDGET.gif mark see-through areas with the transparent index;
reading its palette grey as alpha drew grey bars above the Options slider knobs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Default to Catmull-Rom bicubic scaling, which keeps the original pixels exact

xBR, nearest and bilinear stay available through WINFISH_FILTER.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Smooth the scaled picture with an xBR edge-directed upscaler

WINFISH_FILTER=bilinear keeps the previous filtering.
